headline: High risk of workspace-based prompt injection and data leakage; capability overlap also creates moderate conflict and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP, while the course agent reads/writes files and exposes stdin/stdout plus API endpoints. A shared filesystem or copied outputs can let one agent’s content be treated as instructions by the other. No direct bridge is documented, so this is inferred from documented surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or notebook directory
IF either agent ingests file contents or notebook cells as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP on Cline for shared folders
Use read-only mounts for one agent
Add a manual review step before executing generated instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch sensitive local files: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots, while the course agent handles academic papers, paper metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets. Shared filesystem access plus broad/local egress creates a plausible path for one agent to expose the other’s data, though no direct exfiltration is documented.
conditions: IF the two agents share a writable workspace or mounted secrets directory
IF either agent is allowed to send file contents to external APIs
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared folders
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict outbound network for one agent
Redact sensitive files before either agent reads them

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and execute shells, so concurrent edits to the same workspace can collide. Cline also modifies git state, which increases conflict risk if the course agent writes into the same repo or notebook tree. The profiles do not show locking, so the overlap is real but not maximally dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF Cline is allowed to commit or rewrite git state while the course agent is editing files
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Pause one agent during commits
Use git worktrees or branches
Add file-locking or a single-writer policy

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce browser-derived or code-derived outputs, and the course agent exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints that may consume prior outputs. If the course agent treats Cline’s output as authoritative, errors can propagate into downstream writing or retrieval tasks. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF the course agent feeds Cline-generated text into /api/v1/ask or /api/v1/agentic-ask
IF no verification step checks citations or provenance before reuse
mitigations: Require source verification before reuse
Insert a human approval gate
Log provenance for all imported outputs
Limit the course agent to draft-only mode

E_compliance.rationale: The course agent explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic-paper data, while Cline handles source code and browser screenshots. If regulated or personal data is placed into the course environment, its local-development and Docker-based setup may not match stricter residency or retention expectations. Cline is not cited for a specific compliance gap, so only the course agent is directly implicated.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in the course agent’s notebooks or API inputs
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the same data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the course workspace
Use synthetic or anonymized datasets
Review retention settings before ingestion
Separate compliance-sensitive workloads from both agents
